questions.question: Does MATTER POISE have orders today?
questions.answer: MATTER POISE is newly established and currently has no orders, as confirmed by management on 14 October 2026. Its commercial focus is to turn the team’s joint-module engineering and manufacturing experience into customer evaluation programs and repeat supply.
questions.qualification: Current orders, revenue, evaluation discussions and future sales opportunities are distinct. The no-orders statement should not be broadened into claims about revenue or conversations that the team has not confirmed.
questions.evidence_needed: Track the next milestones through dated evaluations, agreed acceptance criteria, purchase orders and repeat-supply agreements as they develop.

questions.question: Who is the first customer focus?
questions.answer: The target customers are U.S. robotics OEMs, applied-AI or research teams, and automation integrators. The proposed entry is evaluation hardware, scoped engineering and pilot lots, with repeat component or assembly supply as the next step.
questions.qualification: These are target segments and a planned sales path. The newly established company currently has no orders; customer qualification and timing remain to be established program by program.
questions.evidence_needed: Request a dated pipeline by stage and the evaluation-to-supply milestones, with evidence clearly identified as discussions, agreements or orders.

questions.question: How much of the market is actually addressable?
questions.answer: A3 North American robot orders provide industry context. MATTER POISE’s addressable opportunity should be built from compatible customer programs, modules per program, expected adoption and achievable selling prices.
questions.qualification: The cited A3 figures cover complete robots across North America. They are not a U.S. component TAM, and overlapping periods or sectors should not be added together.
questions.evidence_needed: Request a bottom-up account map with segment definitions, integration requirements, annual volumes and buying evidence. Refresh the dated A3 sources for current market totals.

questions.question: Where are the joint modules manufactured today?
questions.answer: The company’s modules are currently predominantly manufactured in China and imported into the U.S. Management plans to build U.S. joint-module production lines gradually, using the existing engineering base to support process transfer.
questions.qualification: The U.S. production lines are a future milestone. Manufacturing location, supplier identity and qualifying origin should be documented for each relevant SKU and lot.
questions.evidence_needed: Request the current manufacturing flow, supplier and quality records, and a phased U.S. production plan with capex, transfer and qualification milestones.

questions.question: Why pursue several robot platforms?
questions.answer: The arm, spherical and quadruped platforms are built around shared large-joint modules and a common hardware architecture. This gives the portfolio a reusable engineering base: different applications can draw on the same core actuation work, limiting duplicated R&D while broadening potential customer uses.
questions.qualification: Reuse does not eliminate platform-specific integration, control, safety and validation work. It is not a claim that every part is shared or that a quantified R&D saving has already been measured.
questions.evidence_needed: Request a platform-to-module map, common interfaces, revision compatibility and separate validation milestones to show how the shared architecture translates into execution.

questions.question: What does a product demo establish?
questions.answer: A demonstration shows prototype behavior and helps explain the intended application. Commercial readiness is assessed separately for each SKU through acceptance testing and repeatable production evidence.
questions.qualification: A clip does not establish qualification for volume production across the portfolio. Integration, tolerances, calibration, reliability and service should be evaluated for the relevant release.
questions.evidence_needed: Request a SKU and revision matrix, acceptance criteria, production records, batch yield, field returns and traceable test results.

questions.question: Where could the manufacturing advantage come from?
questions.answer: The prospective advantage combines self-developed joint architectures, completed technical drawings, shared hardware across platforms, and team experience in embedded control, suppliers and manufacturing transfer. Reuse and disciplined production transfer could support efficient development and scalable delivery.
questions.qualification: This is a capability-based investment case, not a measured claim of superiority over another supplier. Cost and performance comparisons should use equivalent specifications, volumes and service scope.
questions.evidence_needed: Review drawings and interfaces, dated supplier quotations, cycle time, first-pass yield, traceability and warranty assumptions. Compare alternatives respectfully on the same basis.

questions.question: Is $7.5M actual revenue?
questions.answer: No. It is a hypothetical annual component-sales scenario: 5 programs × 500 robots × 12 modules × $250 = $7.5M and 30,000 modules. Every input is a modeling assumption.
questions.qualification: The scenario illustrates how repeat module supply could scale. It is not signed pipeline, a forecast or current revenue; MATTER POISE currently has no orders.
questions.evidence_needed: Request actual revenue records when relevant, customer purchase orders, program timing and cohort assumptions before using the scenario as an operating plan.

questions.question: Are the BOM ranges equivalent to COGS?
questions.answer: No. Published ranges are component budget scenarios. Joint inputs are about $150–500 for larger modules and about $100 for micro drives; the default system scenarios depend on stated quantities and compute choices.
questions.qualification: A fully loaded model also needs end-product assembly, test labor, yield loss, freight, duties, software, warranty and operating expense. Component budgets alone do not establish gross margin.
questions.evidence_needed: Request dated supplier quotations, actual build records and a bridge from BOM to landed good-unit cost, with selling price and warranty assumptions shown separately.

questions.question: Does U.S. sourcing establish compliance?
questions.answer: U.S. supplier spending, component origin and finished-product eligibility are separate questions. The appropriate approach is a traceable BOM and a product-specific review of applicable rules.
questions.qualification: A U.S. invoice or NVIDIA brand alone does not establish qualifying origin or authorization. There is no verified generic chip exemption or domestic-content percentage in this public model.
questions.evidence_needed: Request an origin-documented BOM, supplier declarations, manufacturing flow and SKU-specific regulatory assessment. Recheck the dated primary legal references.

questions.question: What supports the joint-module technology and IP position?
questions.answer: Management reports completed joint-module technical drawings and relevant patent/IP assets being prepared for placement in the U.S. company. The target is to complete that placement before the pre-A financing round, consolidating the engineering foundation for future U.S. manufacturing.
questions.qualification: The target is not a statement that transfer, registration or FTO is complete. Patent grant status, numbers and transfer mechanisms are not specified in this public brief; ownership and freedom to operate need separate evidence.
questions.evidence_needed: Request a controlled drawing index, asset and filing-status schedule, current ownership and contributor records, placement milestones, executed documents when available and appropriate product-specific FTO analysis.

questions.question: What does ROSE do today?
questions.answer: ROSE is in development; management reports an early prototype. The proposed workflow connects concept-to-demo and demo-to-manufacturing, while the public page explains the intended system.
questions.qualification: The explainer illustrates direction rather than a shipped software product or measured productivity gain. The post-2027 commercial stage remains a roadmap milestone.
questions.evidence_needed: Request a dated demonstration, versioned workflow outputs, human-review boundaries, measured baseline comparisons and initial user-validation records.

questions.question: How does the U.S. manufacturing roadmap develop?
questions.answer: Current joint-module supply is predominantly manufactured in China and imported. The next direction is a gradual build-out of U.S. joint-module production lines, followed by greater automation of stable, qualified processes. Existing technical documentation and manufacturing-transfer experience are intended to support that progression.
questions.qualification: Future U.S. lines and a lights-out factory are milestones, not current installed assets. Automation scope should follow demand, process repeatability and good-unit economics.
questions.evidence_needed: Request process-transfer milestones, site and capacity assumptions, capex quotations, qualification criteria and demand-linked expansion gates.

questions.question: What does the 150+ delivery experience mean?
questions.answer: The team materials report 150+ robot deliveries in prior career programs, alongside mechanism, embedded-control, supplier and field-delivery experience. That experience is part of the execution foundation the newly established company aims to bring to its own products.
questions.qualification: Prior-career deliveries are distinct from MATTER POISE shipments or current orders. The company currently has no orders, and specific prior responsibilities can be reviewed through permitted references.
questions.evidence_needed: Request role-based, dated program references, scope of responsibility and manufacturing-transfer evidence that can be shared appropriately.

questions.question: What milestones is the financing intended to support?
questions.answer: Management confirms an approximately $8–10M seed fundraising planning range as of 14 October 2026. The $10M example allocates capital across equipment, team and operations, R&D and transfer, and working capital or contingency.
questions.qualification: This is a working financing plan, not money raised or confirmed terms. Runway, cap table, valuation and commitments require current team confirmation.
questions.evidence_needed: Request a monthly cash plan, cap table, proposed terms and milestones tied to evaluations, joint-module IP placement before pre-A, product qualification and repeatable delivery.
